correctness.rationale: The global-bit-complement orientation lemma proves any binary code lies in the complete unbordered 0-to-1 candidate vertex set. For each (n,d), n=2..11 and d=2..n, the pairwise compatibility relation exactly matches non-overlap plus Hamming distance, hence maximum size equals maximum clique. Greedy proper coloring bounds every clique in the remaining search graph and makes the recursive upper bounds rigorous. Exhaustive traversal computes all 55 maxima, matched by explicit valid word sets in certificates.json. Independent C++ string/bitset implementation reproduces all 55. Nothing is claimed for larger n.

originality.rationale: The 55 exact optimum sizes jointly constrain cross-bifix-free and aligned Hamming-error-correcting binary codes, and are not implied by published unconstrained optimum tables, existing asymptotic bounds, or error-correcting constructions in the inspected relevant papers. The first strict distance-two penalty is at n=10 (24 to 23); at n=11 the sharp distance-three value is 14. Indexed searches found no exact Hamming frontier. A prior unindexed exact table remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The simultaneous design problem is natural for self-synchronizing blocks that also correct aligned substitutions. The 55 certified optima close the complete short-block tradeoff, expose a first nontrivial distance-two penalty at n=10 (24 down to 23), and determine the exact one-substitution-correcting n=11 capacity (14), beyond d=1 constructions. These are technically useful capacity benchmarks, not a small arbitrary subset of a pre-existing tabulation.
